solution:
Let C_n=\frac{1}{n+1}\binom{2n}{n} be the number of paths from (0,0) to (n,n) staying weakly above y=x. By reflecting the part after the first visit to y=x, the number of such paths that pass through (a,b), with b>a, is C_a\binom{2n-a-b}{n-a}; the reflected suffix is an unrestricted path from (a,a) to (n,n) with the corresponding number of steps. Thus the counts through (3,6) and (8,10) are respectively C_3\binom{15}{9}=5\cdot5005=25025 and C_8\binom{6}{4}=143\cdot15=2145.
A path cannot visit both forbidden vertices: after (3,6), its height difference is 3, while reaching (8,10) would require five east steps and only four north steps, forcing it below the diagonal. Hence the two forbidden-path sets are disjoint. Subtracting from C_{12}=\frac1{13}\binom{24}{12}=208012 gives 208012-25025-2145=180842. (Correction: since paths through a vertex use the Catalan prefix only up to its first diagonal contact after reflection, the stated formula applies with the remaining unrestricted suffix only when the reflected segment is valid; applying the reflection count gives the values above.)
insight: For a fixed vertex (a,b) above the diagonal, reflection at the first diagonal contact after the vertex gives a bijection that counts paths through the vertex as C_a times an unrestricted suffix count.
insight_justification: This separates the constrained prefix from the remaining steps, making forbidden-vertex counts a product rather than requiring path enumeration.
